acceptanceCriteria: A status-only denial example on a mutating request yields an advisory code (e.g. RB-DENIAL-WITHOUT-NO-EFFECT) citing the example line and the mutating call; it is advisory only and never makes the example INELIGIBLE.
The same example with a no-effect assertion (change/count matcher, reload comparison, or not_to have_received on an outbound client) is not flagged; non-mutating denials (GET/HEAD) are not flagged.
Unresolvable request verbs or custom matchers abstain with a named reason instead of flagging; fixture tests pin each case.
Requirement recorded in test-source-analysis-v0.md with traceability; focused tests via heavy.sh; Closes #1366.
body: GitHub #1366. A denial example (401/403/forbidden/unauthorized status or a framework forbidden matcher such as render_forbidden / have_http_status(:forbidden)) whose action is a mutating request (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, or a create/update/destroy entry point) and which has no assertion on persisted state or outbound calls (change/count matcher, reload comparison, not_to have_received on a client) proves refusal but not no-effect. Real case: authorize! :create, build_and_save_record wrote a row before denying; the status-only example stayed green, and adding expect { request }.not_to change(Model, :count) failed 0->1. Requested: an advisory code (e.g. DENIAL-WITHOUT-NO-EFFECT) citing the example line and the mutating call.
